transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-12-24 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Miguel Torres (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (CTO, BlueWave), Priya Rao (ML Eng), Derek Liu (Platform Eng)

Summary: quick POC weekly check-in focused on staging access, credentials, and a targeted latency/QPS triage following the Friday micro-bursts. We validated that the staging gateway is reachable, flagged an egress/NAT issue that impacted KV cache priming, and agreed higher-priority next steps: run formal 10k token burst on dedicated pool, share security docs, and set a network deep-dive next week.

Topics: staging creds, VPC egress, KMS/SAML questions, p99 latency, continuous batching, quant profile for embeddings, autoscaler tuning, benchmark CSVs, handoff to CS.

Transcript:
[00:00] Laura: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick roll call, we got the usual group?
[00:05] Samir: yeah Samir here, Priya and Derek on my side too. morning.
[00:07] Priya: hey.
[00:09] Miguel: Miguel here, Redwood SE. good to see you all.
[00:11] Laura: sweet. objective for today is short — confirm staging access, review the brief bench runs from friday, and prioritize any infra triage.
[00:20] Derek: on the access side, we tried to spin up the staging gateway but hit outbound rules. looks like our NAT isn't letting the callbacks reach Redwood endpoints.
[00:28] Miguel: okay that matches what we saw in logs — we saw partial connections, and the KV cache priming failed so cold starts were way higher than expected. kind of a double whammy.
[00:36] Priya: yeah, from the model perspective p50 was okay but p95/p99 spiked which is what worried us for latency SLOs. we saw token latencies creeping to the 800ms range for some sequences.
[00:46] Laura: ugh. can you show the exact request path? is this hosted or dedicated pool in the staging env?
[00:52] Derek: staging is on dedicated-ish config — we pinned to the dedicated pool you provisioned, but our egress NAT was misconfigured so the control-plane callbacks couldn't fetch telemetry metrics and the client-side retries caused a little backpressure.
[01:05] Miguel: one note here — when KV cache priming fails, subsequent requests cause full KV recompute; that alone can add ~200-400ms depending on sequence length. and then if the autoscaler is slow to spin up, you get queuing.
[01:18] Samir: makes sense. so the immediate fix is NAT/egress, but are there tuning knobs we should flip on the Redwood side to protect against priming failures?
[01:26] Miguel: yes — two quick mitigations: 1) enable prefix caching persistency for session tokens so the cache survives small restarts, and 2) set the continuous-batching window to a slightly longer tail to absorb jitter. we can suggest exact values after we see the Friday CSV.
[01:40] Priya: about continuous batching — we are concerned about latency for short-chunk QA queries. is there a tradeoff if we increase batching window?
[01:46] Miguel: right, so for short queries you lose some tail latency if you wait too long. but you get better throughput and cost. typical compromise is 10-15ms additional batching window for high qps paths that are tolerant, and keep low-latency routes uncached or route to a separate low-latency pool.
[02:02] Laura: that ties into the routing policy we discussed — can we keep a low-latency hosted fallback for critical calls and use dedicated for the heavy embedding/rerank traffic?
[02:11] Miguel: absolutely, policy-based routing is supported. and we can set automatic fallback to hosted (or a smaller low-latency variant) if dedicated capacity saturates.
[02:18] Derek: ok that helps. on the security front Priya's team ran the preliminary SOC2 checklist — we need the KMS integration details and SAML metadata so our security team can sign off.
[02:27] Laura: I will share the SOC2 pack and SAML setup doc after this call; you'll have the SAML metadata and KMS details — note that our Private option supports customer-managed KMS/HSM if you need key isolation.
[02:39] Samir: is customer-managed KMS available for the pilot or only for private deployments?
[02:43] Miguel: for the hosted POC we support envelope encryption with customer KMS in the Private plane; for dedicated pools we can support a KMS integration if we have the right IAM grant from your side. it's not fully automatic but we've done it for other customers in pilot.
[02:58] Priya: small clarification on logs — do you expose token-level telemetry or only aggregates? the security team asked about PII redaction.
[03:05] Laura: we emit per-request traces (with sampling) and token-level cost breakdowns, but we can turn off raw input retention and only keep hashes for auditing. we also support redaction at ingest if you want.
[03:18] Derek: good. back to the bench results from Friday — Miguel, can you summarize the findings?
[03:22] Miguel: sure — short summary: single-worker dedicated pool, sequence avg 64 tokens for rerank workload, under synthetic load we hit peak qps ~220 with p95 320ms, p99 620-780ms. KV priming events caused p99 to spike to ~1.2s in a couple of runs. embeddings workload with quant profile Q4_0 hit expected throughput but had slightly higher decode latency.
[03:43] Priya: those numbers sound in line with what we feared. the p99s are what will bite for SLAs.
[03:48] Miguel: agreed — we recommended two follow-ups: 1) re-run with warming traffic to fully prime KV and measure steady-state p99; 2) run a burst test with long-context (10k tokens) to check memory/kv eviction patterns.
[04:03] Laura: and those are the tasks we'll take on — Miguel will run the long-context burst on the dedicated pool and attach the CSVs.
[04:09] Samir: timeline on that? we want to validate before EOM.
[04:12] Miguel: we can run it over the weekend and share results Monday — aiming for 2026-12-28.
[04:17] Priya: one more thing — our prompt set includes rerank followed by short QA in sequence, so the mixed workload matters. we should ensure caching persists across the rerank->qa hop.
[04:27] Miguel: yeah that pattern benefits a sticky session / prefix caching config. we'll send a recommended config.
[04:32] Derek: network deep dive — we found that our egress path uses a NAT gateway in a single AZ which got throttled. we should probably add a second NAT or use managed egress so callbacks succeed.
[04:42] Miguel: can you also share the traceroute to the Redwood ingress? in a couple of cases DNS resolutions fell back to older IPs which caused small timeouts.
[04:50] Derek: we'll pull that and dump to the ticket.
[04:53] Laura: perfect. quick run through of open blockers: 1) staged service account + IP allowlist (blocks gating), 2) KMS/SAML docs for compliance sign-off, 3) bench re-run for steady-state numbers. any others?
[05:05] Priya: just one — telemetry retention requirements. our compliance wants logs retained for 90 days but with redaction. is that configurable?
[05:12] Laura: yes, retention tiers are configurable; we can offer 90-days with encrypted-at-rest artifacts and only hashed raw inputs. will include in the security doc.
[05:20] Samir: good. competitively, our security team asked if you've done integrations similar to Anthropic or OpenAI migrations — they're looking for references.
[05:29] Laura: we can provide anonymized case notes and performance comparisons; not customer-identifying but shows our TCO and latency tradeoffs.
[05:35] Miguel: and on performance tradeoffs: quantization for embeddings will drop footprint but may add 5-15% latency variance; we tend to recommend Q4_0 for embeddings and Q8 or Q6 for decoder where latency is critical.
[05:48] Priya: can you quantify the cost delta? our finance wants ballpark per-1M tokens.
[05:53] Laura: I'll attach the pricing sheet but ballpark for dedicated pooled workloads it's X$/1M tokens for the heavy model, and with Q4 you can reduce GPU-hours by ~20% — I'll include ranges rather than exact.
[06:03] Derek: on the autoscaler front we saw slow spin-up; is there a warm pool option?
[06:08] Miguel: yes — warm pool / burst capacity is available as a config: keep N warm replicas that are cheaper but can take traffic immediately; that reduces cold-start but increases baseline cost. we can show tradeoffs with the benchmark CSV.
[06:21] Samir: ok let's list who owns what: Miguel does the bench and autoscaler proposal; Derek gets access and egress rules; Laura shares security/pricing docs; Priya will send real prompt traffic; Samir will brief execs after we have steady-state p99.
[06:37] Laura: awesome — also proposing a follow-up network call with Derek and Miguel next week; I'll loop in the CS manager after we have bench results to discuss pilot expansion.
[06:47] Priya: quick question — for SSO does Redwood support IdP-initiated flows or only SP-initiated?
[06:52] Laura: both; we support IdP-initiated SAML and OIDC flows. we'll include SAML metadata.
[06:58] Miguel: small transcription note — the Friday run showed KV "cash" priming in logs, that's actually KV cache. sometimes transcription turned it into cash in the CSV.
[07:06] (laughter)
[07:09] Samir: thanks for the call. any other items?
[07:12] Laura: that's all from us. recap in the notes: run long-context burst, fix staging egress, share security docs, schedule network deep-dive.
[07:20] Derek: we'll prioritize egress and get the account details to Laura by tomorrow.
[07:25] Miguel: I'll kick off the burst tonight.
[07:28] Laura: great, we'll regroup after results — happy holidays everyone and we'll talk Monday.

End of transcript.
